block2_rope_positions_slot1_k_oracle.description: K-slot (slot 1) bit-identity + sign-flip RED control added to every CPU (4) and CUDA (4) identity leg, plus an independent closed-form dK check in the CUDA bwd test. All GREEN on the real kernel.

block1_flash_arm_encoder_level_oracle.description: cuda-kernel-guide.md SS3.3 three-way oracle (flash-bf16 vs block-bf16 vs f32 reference) on a real ModernBERT-large checkpoint, Gaussian-init LoRA (rank=16, alpha=32, target=Wqkv), seed-keyed synthetic ids, pooled-embedding + step-0 dL/d(layer0 Wqkv LoRA B) gradient.
block1_flash_arm_encoder_level_oracle.bound: err(flash, f32) <= K * err(block, f32), K = 1.5
block1_flash_arm_encoder_level_oracle.bound_derivation: Auditor's own hand-run oracle on this checkpoint measured err(flash,f32)=5.71e-2 vs err(block,f32)=9.11e-2 -- flash already closer to truth. K=1.5 keeps 1.5*err(block) well above flash's own measured distance (healthy bf16-noise margin) while still reddening the K-unrotated mutant (auditor: 6.42e-1) and window-dropped mutant (auditor: 4.73e-1) many-fold over the realized bound.

b8_s512.note: grad err magnitudes are large in absolute terms because the LoRA-B gradient reference values are themselves near-zero for many elements at this random Gaussian init (relative-L1 blows up); flash and block track each other and the bound holds -- the qualitative comparison (not the raw magnitude) is what the oracle gates on.

k_unrotated_b8_s512.note: matches the auditor's own '8-11x mutants' expectation

bad_softmax_scale_b8_s512.note: class-sweep advisory: softmax_scale wiring quantity, cheap to add given the K-unrotated harness already existed

dq_accum_measured_live_a100c.description: Live-measured (not estimated) via jammi_kernels::flash::{CuSeqlens, dq_accum_splits, VarlenGeometry::dq_accum_len} at deterministic=true -- the ONE flash-only backward allocation this branch's own module doc already names.

b24_s512_h16_sanity_check_vs_module_doc.module_doc_citation: ~63 MB at B=24,S=512 -- matches to within rounding, confirming the measurement methodology

dq_accum_measured_live_a100c.verdict: dq_accum is real, flash-only, deterministic-backward VRAM, but at ~21 MB it is TWO ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE too small to explain the 1.8-2.7 GB b8-s512 delta. It is a confirmed, precisely-quantified contributor, NOT the dominant one.

fused_masks_local_band_common_mode_waste.description: Confirmed by reading forward_hidden_with_lengths: fused_masks (FusedAttentionMasks::build, an allocate+broadcast_add+cast at [batch,heads-ish,seq,seq] scale) and local_band are built unconditionally whenever self.training, REGARDLESS of whether the flash decision Holds for every layer -- the flash arm never reads either. This is COMMON-MODE waste (paid by BOTH arms identically), so it cannot explain the flash-vs-block DELTA on its own, but it is real, attributable, wasted allocation on the flash leg specifically.
fused_masks_local_band_common_mode_waste.why_not_attempted_this_round: Skipping the build requires relaxing TWO separate, currently-unconditional, already-tested contract checks: (1) ModernBertAttention::forward's 'fused_masks required whenever self.training' typed-refusal (doc table + training_attention_forward_without_fused_masks_is_a_typed_refusal), and (2) forward_training_attention's 'is_local && local_band.is_none() -> Err' check, which fires BEFORE the flash-cascade decision is even consulted. A safe relaxation is possible (decide_flash_admission's outcome==Holds, combined with a side-effect-free replica of admission::op_is_disabled via the public disabled_ops_requested() getter, deterministically predicts every layer will dispatch Fused), but implementing and re-verifying it touches a widely-tested invariant this file's own 'KNOWN GAP, NOT FIXED THIS ROUND (P3 fix round 4, B4 -- deferred a THIRD time)' comment already flags as deferred twice by the original authors for the same reason: real (if small) error-path risk without pod-iteration budget to verify safely. Not attempted this round; flagged as an open item for the lead, not silently dropped.
